steps.context: Same raw counts and metadata as T1S1. Batches are balanced across condition per the data context (6 treated/6 control split evenly across 2 batches), which permits including batch as a covariate in the DESeq2 design without confounding condition.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 profiled genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) kidney samples when the model adjusts for the two known, condition-balanced processing batches?
constraints: Design formula must be ~ batch + condition, with condition as the final term so its coefficient is directly testable
Use apeglm or equivalent shrinkage (lfcShrink) for reported log2FoldChange values rather than raw MLE estimates
Do not drop the batch term even if PCA in T1S1 shows a weak batch effect — the design specifies known batches to adjust for
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design formula ~ batch + condition on raw integer counts
Full results table (gene symbol, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) exported for all 12000 genes
Significant gene set defined at padj < 0.05 (and reported also at padj < 0.1 as a secondary threshold) with counts of up- and down-regulated genes stated
MA plot and volcano plot produced from the results
Independent filtering / dispersion diagnostics (dispersion plot) reported to confirm model fit is reasonable for n=6 per group

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treated vs control DE genes
caveats: With ~12000 background genes rather than genome-wide (~20000+), pathway gene set coverage will be partial; report the fraction of each pathway's genes actually present in the background
If the WikiPathways human GMT reference is absent at run time, report the gap rather than substituting an unrelated organism's gene sets
steps.context: Input is the full DESeq2 results table (gene symbol, log2FoldChange, stat, padj) from T1S2 for all 12000 genes. Reference: WikiPathways human pathway gene sets (GMT, HGNC gene symbols) at the wikipathways-human managed reference (2026.07.10 snapshot) — confirm presence before use since references are not guaranteed at run time.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are over-represented among genes differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples (from T1S2)?
constraints: Gene symbols in counts.csv must be matched to the HGNC symbols used in the WikiPathways GMT without further ID mapping (both are human gene symbols)
Prefer a ranked GSEA (using DESeq2 stat or log2FoldChange) over a simple overrepresentation test on an arbitrary padj cutoff, to use the full ranked gene list rather than only the significant subset
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run separately (or combined with sign-aware ranking) on up-regulated and down-regulated significant gene sets from T1S2, and/or a full pre-ranked GSEA using the DE test statistic across all 12000 genes
Uses the WikiPathways human gene sets (HGNC symbols) resolved from the reference store
Reports enriched pathway name, WikiPathways ID, gene overlap/leading-edge genes, p-value and FDR-adjusted q-value
States explicitly if the reference gene set file is unavailable at run time and what was substituted or omitted as a result

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (salmon-derived raw integer gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol, 12 samples) from human kidney tissue, comparing 6 treated vs 6 control samples with two known processing batches balanced across conditions (batch is not confounded with condition, so it can be safely modeled as a covariate). The plan runs a standard count-based differential expression workflow (DESeq2) with batch included in the design formula to remove technical variation while preserving condition effect estimation, followed by diagnostic QC (library size, PCA colored by batch/condition) to confirm the batch-balanced design behaves as expected, and functional interpretation of the resulting DE gene list via pathway enrichment using the WikiPathways human gene sets available in the reference store. No translational/clinical outcome data is present, so no biomarker, safety, or PK/PD steps are included.
